subject: Acceptance Report: Reserved Pool Growth Validation & Monitoring Runbook
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved pool growth — post-renewal handoff and load window

Hey team,

Per the signed renewal (DL-2027-0147), Atlas' Dedicated capacity was expanded overnight: reserved pool increased by 12x A100 equivalent GPUs (net +9 from prior commit due to rebalancing). SLA amendments for throughput (75M tokens/day baseline with 99th pct latency target <= 450ms for short-form gen) are in the contract addendum.

I'm attaching the execution plan we used for the provisioning and the runbook we'll follow for the acceptance window: reserved-pool-load-plan.csv; post-renewal-runbook.md (attached).

Request: Can ops run the acceptance load during the agreed window (2027-04-13 02:00 UTC) and capture token/sec, 50/95/99 latencies, tail behavior, and GPU utilization per card? Flag any 95/99 spikes and note whether KV/prefix cache warm-up materially impacts throughput.

Stakeholders to include on the run: Atlas SREs (Beth, Kate) for live validation and Redwood support (Mateo + Rafael). I'll be on standby for contract confirmation items.

Thanks,

—Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: reserved-pool-load-plan.csv; post-renewal-runbook.md
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Beth Green <beth.green@atlas-enterprises.com>, Kate Long <kate.long@atlas-enterprises.com>
Date: 2027-04-13 03:50:32 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved pool growth — post-renewal handoff and load window

Attaching the run results from the 02:00 UTC acceptance window (load-results-summary.pdf). TL;DR: baseline throughput met and slightly exceeded the committed target under steady-state synthetic traffic; 95th latency averaged 380ms for 1k-token tails; 99th saw intermittent spikes up to ~820ms during cache-warm periods (first 6 minutes of each prefix group).

Key numbers (summary):
- Sustained tokens/sec (aggregate): 18.6k TPS
- Per-GPU average utilization: 64% (with autoscaling headroom intact)
- 50/95/99-latency (short gen prompts): 120ms / 380ms / 820ms
- Error rate: 0.03% (transient backend retries, all recovered)

Observations and actionables:
1) Prefix/KV cache warm-up accounts for the 99th spikes. We recommend a short pre-warm wave (low-cost synthetic prefix hits) before heavy production windows.
2) Batching window at current default (8ms) is a good balance. If Atlas wants lower 99th latency during peak, reducing the batching window to 4ms reduces throughput ~4% but lowers 99th to ~620ms in lab.
3) I/O on the shared NVMe persisted checkpoint caused a couple of ~50ms jitter events — we isolated them and increased prefetch threads in the runtime.

Next steps: Rafael will deliver a monitoring playbook and set up the Datadog dashboard with the SLI breakouts. If Atlas signs off, we can mark the expansion as Accepted and transition to standard monitoring cadence.

Thanks — attaching load-results-summary.pdf for full logs.

—Mateo Alvarez
Technical Program Manager, Customer Success (QoS)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: load-results-summary.pdf

Hi Mateo / Lauren,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and detailed notes. We reviewed the load-results-summary.pdf — the sustained throughput numbers meet our expectations and the transient 99th spikes are acceptable given the cache warm-up explanation. Atlas signs off on the expansion as complete. Please mark DL-2027-0147 as Accepted in HubSpot and move the project to steady-state monitoring.

One request: can Redwood add two alert tiers in Datadog — one for immediate SRE paging at 99th > 900ms sustained for 5m, and a lower-priority ticket if 99th between 700-900ms for 10m? We want a noise-resistant escalation.

Appreciate the team effort.

Atlas Enterprises

Subject: Monitoring playbook and acceptance artifacts for DL-2027-0147

Beth / Lauren / Mateo,

Attached is the monitoring-checklist.xlsx and a short monitoring playbook excerpt below. I've also created the Datadog dashboard and a HubSpot activity: https://app.datadog.com/dashboard/atlas-reserved-pool (dashboard) and https://hubspot.com/deal/DL-2027-0147 (HubSpot).

Monitoring playbook (excerpt):
- SLOs and alerts:
  • Pager: 99th latency > 900ms sustained for 5m OR error rate > 0.5%
  • Ticket only: 99th latency 700-900ms for 10m OR GPU util > 90% for 15m without autoscaler response
- On-call steps:
  1) Check load spike source (prefix warm-up vs production pattern)
  2) Trigger cache pre-warm job if warm-up identified
  3) If error rate persists, failover to fallback model variant per routing policy
  4) Escalate to Infra if NVMe I/O errors are present (see attachment notes)
- Reporting cadence: daily summaries for the first 72 hours post-acceptance, then weekly for 4 weeks, then monthly.

I'll update the DocuSign closure link in HubSpot once you're fully signed off.

Regards,

—Rafael Mendes
Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
